title: Condition Report
description: Rubella recites inventory like a vow. Clause four never arrives. Solo cello, una corda piano, no drums until the last line. Pairing for The Overnight Conservator.
stylePrompt: Museum-hushed chamber noir at 64 BPM. Solo cello and una corda piano only — no drums, no kick, no hi-hat until the final spoken line. Marble dust replaces tape hiss as the texture. Room tone is HVAC and a security monitor's faint sync buzz, not mains hum. Soft breathy female vocal, Rubella, close-mic, almost spoken — she recites condition-report clauses like a vow rather than paperwork. No belting, no vibrato; the intimacy is procedural. Dark top end, real gallery reverb, never bright. **Structural flaw:** the condition report she dictates skips from clause 3 to clause 5, every verse, every time — clause 4 never arrives. Nobody in the song notices or fixes it. Mood: 3 a.m. classical wing; she is the conservator and the exhibit. Runtime ~2:00–2:20. Use the Rubella voice.
lyrics:
[Intro — HVAC / dust]
(una corda figure, cello holds one note; no pulse yet)

[Verse 1]
Clause one: the surface shows a hairline stress
Clause two: acceptable, given the address
Clause three: the varnish caught the flash and held
Clause five: recommend we leave it as it fell

[Pre-Chorus]
I initial in a color that will not stay
The marble keeps the hour better than I do

[Chorus]
I'm the conservator, you're the exhibit
Hold the glass steady, I'll note the damage
Every report I file skips a number
It's the only clause I ever manage
To lose on purpose

[Verse 2]
Clause one: a fracture older than the gala
Clause two: the forearm came away without a fight
Clause three: the flute is at the correct height
Clause five: do not attempt to make it right

[Pre-Chorus]
I initial in a color that will not stay
The marble keeps the hour better than I do

[Chorus]
I'm the conservator, you're the exhibit
Hold the glass steady, I'll note the damage
Every report I file skips a number
It's the only clause I ever manage
To lose on purpose

[Bridge]
The second statue has my shoes
The monitor is snow
If clause four was a confession
I already know

[Final Chorus]
I'm the conservator, you're the exhibit
Hold the glass steady, I'll note the damage
Every report I file skips a number
It's the only clause I ever manage

[Spoken — last line; one soft stamp as the only percussion]
Leave it as it fell.
notes:
## Production notes
- **Episode placement:** One-panel gag score for gag #6 **The Overnight Conservator** (`notes/one-panel-gags.md`). Also works as EyeWash "gallery after hours" insert, sibling hour to *Master Control, 4 AM*.
- **Voice:** Rubella, close, almost spoken. No second voice. No Continuity Voice.
- **Structural flaw:** Clause 4 is omitted in every verse. Do not "fix" it in a later pass. Do not let a backing vocal supply the missing number.
- **Arrangement:** Cello + una corda only until the last spoken line, which may take a single marble-stamp / form-stamp hit. No drums before that.
- **Sibling tracks:** *After Is a Floor* (bureaucracy as destination) and *Complaint Window, Deep Field*'s manners family — this one is inventory, not transit. Do not duplicate *Rinse Cycle* (sign-off owns the institutional anthem).
- **Runtime target:** 2:00–2:20. Cheap to picture: one gallery, one statue, one spotlight.
- **Chords (suggested):** Verse `i – VI – III – v` (Am–F–C–Em) landing on v instead of iv — the missing iv is clause 4. Chorus `VI – III – iv – i` (F–C–Dm–Am). Bridge holds III for two extra bars.
- **Melodic motifs:** Spoken-sung falling minor 2nd on *clause five*; cello answers a fifth below and does not resolve. Title never appears as a sung hook — she names her job, not the form.
